title: Set Time Machine backup destination
summary: Configure where Time Machine saves your backups. You can specify a local disk or a network share.

steps.explain: Set a local HFS+ drive as the backup destination. Replace <DISK_MOUNT_POINT> with the path to your mounted drive (e.g., /Volumes/MyBackup).

placeholders.name: DISK_MOUNT_POINT
placeholders.description: The path to the mounted drive you want to use for backups.

alternatives.explain: Set a network share (APFS or SMB) as the backup destination. Replace <SHARE_URL> with the full URL including credentials.

placeholders.name: SHARE_URL
placeholders.description: The URL of the network share, e.g., smb://user:password@host/share

alternatives.explain: Append a destination to the existing list of backup destinations instead of replacing it.

placeholders.name: DESTINATION
placeholders.description: The path or URL of the destination to add.

rollback.explain: To revert to the default destination or remove the current one, you typically need to use the Time Machine preferences in System Settings, as tmutil does not provide a simple 'unset' command in this page. Alternatively, you can set a different valid destination.

placeholders.name: NEW_DESTINATION
placeholders.description: The path or URL of the new destination to set.

warnings: Changing the backup destination will stop backups to the previous location. Ensure the new destination is formatted correctly and has enough space.
